summary: Tides Cove Point, Newfoundland: a diaphone fog alarm from 1912, a light from 1915, the 1941 Larpool lifeboat landing, and a Coast Guard station listed as staffed in 2019, with the grounds open.

light.fog_signal: horn, one 4 s blast every 60 s (CCG list); diaphone fog alarm from 1912 (LF)

structures.type: square skeleton tower with octagonal upper portion
structures.note: LF gives 1992 and 11.3 m (CCG list agrees on height); Rowlett gives 1993 and 9.5 m.

structures.type: one-storey combination light and fog signal building with a tower at one corner; replaced an earlier wooden fog-signal building
structures.note: Built by S. J. Scott with two dwellings for $67,300 (LF). Rowlett: lantern later moved to a concrete fog-signal building.

staffing.note: DFO page (date modified 2019-09-24) lists Tides Cove Point among 23 staffed lightstations. LF: de-staffed 1992, re-staffed 2003.

access.note: Listed as staffed in 2019 (DFO): the keepers' home and workplace. LF and Rowlett: grounds open, tower closed. Keep to the grounds described as open; do not climb the tower.

events.note: Diaphone fog alarm, air compressed by an oil engine; station then had a keeper's dwelling, engine house and store house (LF).
Larpool, British steamer, torpedoed by U-208 on 2 Nov 1941 (uboat.net). LF places the attack about 250 miles ESE of Cape Race; uboat.net says 150 miles.
Five men from the Larpool's lifeboat reached the shore at Tide's Cove on 13 Nov 1941 (LF). uboat.net instead gives a six-man boat landing near Burin on 10 Nov.
Combination light and fog signal building with two dwellings, by S. J. Scott, $67,300 (LF).
Present square skeleton tower erected (LF). Rowlett gives 1993.
Station de-staffed and automated when the tower went up (LF).

wrecks.outcome: British steamer torpedoed by U-208 (uboat.net). Five men from her lifeboat came ashore at Tide's Cove on 13 Nov 1941 (LF); uboat.net gives a six-man boat landing near Burin on 10 Nov.

notes_for_editor: 1) Tower date and height: LF says the present tower was erected in 1992 (11.3 m); Rowlett says 1993 (9.5 m). The record's event 1993 'built' comes from Rowlett; the story uses LF's 1992 and the CCG's 11.3 m. Not verified on site. 2) Larpool: LF puts the sinking about 250 miles ESE of Cape Race; uboat.net says 150 miles. LF says five men drifted eleven days to Tide's Cove, arriving 13 Nov; uboat.net says a six-man boat made landfall near Burin on 10 Nov. The story reports both and does not choose. Newspapers.py found no 1941 coverage in Chronicling America. The IWM sound-archive record (object 80010577) of an officer's recollections of the Larpool was read for its catalogue description only and is not cited. 3) Staffing: the station record says staffed as of 2010 with a check flag. DFO's staffed list (date modified 2019-09-24) names Tides Cove Point, which can clear the 2010 check but is not a 2026 site check. 4) Keepers: all names come from LF, which gives no document for them. Gary Antle, John Kavanagh and Bob Power are living-person risk: named only as LF prints them, no further detail. Irene (a keeper's child, now an adult) is named only by first name in the story; LF gives her married surname, which is not used. 5) Nothing read says what hazard the 1912 fog alarm was for. Not stated in the story.
